asks: Which route gives Silo the file changes of a computer from outside?
answer: The engine compares the disk at each checkpoint with the one before, from outside the computer. Nothing is slowed while the computer runs. A file fact then says between which two checkpoints the file changed. A file created and deleted between two checkpoints is not in the record, and the record says its file facts have that grain. A rename is written as a delete and a create, since the trial took 4,939 of 10,000 deletes for renames. The engine does not serve the work folders itself: the trials measured builds 1.6 to 2.1 times slower and work on small files 12.6 to 192 times slower. To find out: the same on a macOS computer, which no trial has run; whether what the computer has not yet saved to its disk can be caught without running a program inside; whether a file written and put back with its change time reset can be caught through the blocks written; reading only the blocks written since the last checkpoint, which took 0.1 s on the Mac; and how the host reads a disk that a hostile agent wrote.
